title.zh: 卷一百四十六 列傳第三十三: 耶律楚材 粘合重山 楊惟中
title.en: Volume 146 Biographies 33: Yelü Chucai, Zhanhezhongshan, Yang Weizhong
title.raw: 卷一百四十六 列傳第三十三: 耶律楚材 粘合重山 楊惟中 Volume 146 Biographies 33: Yelü Chucai, Zhanhezhongshan, Yang Weizhong

sentences.zh: 耶律楚材子鑄附

translations.literal: Appendix: Yelü Chucai's son Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Yelü Zhu, son of Yelü Chucai.

sentences.zh: 耶律楚材，字晉卿，遼東丹王突欲八世孫。

translations.literal: Yelü Chucai, style name Jinqing, was an eighth-generation descendant of the Liao Dongdan King Tuyü.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Chucai, whose style was Jinqing, was an eighth-generation descendant of Tuyü, the Dongdan king of Liao.

sentences.zh: 父履，以學行事金世宗，特見親任，終尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His father Lü, known for learning and conduct under Jin Emperor Shizong, was especially favored and trusted, and ended as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lü won favor under Jin Emperor Shizong through learning and upright conduct, rose to unusual trust, and ended his career as right vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 楚材生三歲而孤，母楊氏教之學。

translations.literal: Chucai was orphaned at three; his mother, Lady Yang, taught him.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai lost his father at the age of three, and his mother, the Lady Yang, saw to his education.

sentences.zh: 及長，博極群書，旁通天文、地理、律曆、術數及釋老、醫卜之說，下筆為文，若宿構者。

translations.literal: When grown, he mastered all books and was versed besides in astronomy, geography, calendrics, numerology, and the teachings of Buddhism, Daoism, medicine, and divination; when he took up the brush to write, it was as if the text had been prepared beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he mastered the classics and also astronomy, geography, calendrics, numerology, Buddhist and Daoist doctrine, medicine, and divination. When he wrote, the prose seemed already composed in his mind.

sentences.zh: 金制，宰相子例試補省掾。

translations.literal: Under Jin regulations, sons of grand councilors were by precedent examined and appointed as secretariat clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Jin custom allowed sons of grand councilors to enter the secretariat by a special examination rather than the regular civil-service route.

sentences.zh: 楚材欲試進士科，章宗詔如舊制。

translations.literal: Chucai wished to take the jinshi examination; Emperor Zhangzong ordered that the old regulations apply.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai wanted to sit for the jinshi examination, and Emperor Zhangzong permitted him to follow the usual procedure.

sentences.zh: 問以疑獄數事，時同試者十七人，楚材所對獨優，遂辟為掾。

translations.literal: He was questioned on several doubtful legal cases; of the seventeen taking the examination at the time, Chucai's answers alone were superior, and he was thereupon appointed a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The examiners put several knotty legal cases to him. Among the seventeen candidates, only Chucai's answers stood out, and he was appointed a secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 後仕為開州同知。

translations.literal: Later he served as vice prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as vice prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，宣宗遷汴，完顏福興行尚書事，留守燕，辟為左右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, when Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, Wanyan Fuxing acted as Director of the Secretariat and remained to guard Yan; he appointed Chucai Outer Vice Director of the Left and Right Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou, when Emperor Xuanzong moved the court to Bian, Wanyan Fuxing stayed in Yan as acting director of the secretariat and recruited Chucai as an outer vice director of the left and right offices.

sentences.zh: 太祖定燕，聞其名，召見之。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Yan, he heard Chucai's name and summoned him for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu secured Yan, he heard of Chucai and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 楚材身長八尺，美髯宏聲。

translations.literal: Chucai was eight chi tall, with a fine beard and a resonant voice.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai stood eight chi in height, with a splendid beard and a booming voice.

sentences.zh: 帝偉之，曰：「遼、金世仇，朕為汝雪之。

translations.literal: The emperor admired him and said, "Liao and Jin were hereditary foes; I shall avenge you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and said, "Liao and Jin were hereditary enemies. I will avenge that wrong for you."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣父祖嘗委質事之，既為之臣，敢仇君耶！

translations.literal: He replied, "My father and grandfather once pledged themselves to serve them; having become their subjects, how dare I hold a grudge against my lord!"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai answered, "My father and grandfather once pledged themselves to Jin. Once one has become a subject, how can one turn against one's lord?"

sentences.zh: 」帝重其言，處之左右，遂呼楚材曰吾圖撒合里而不名，吾圖撒合裡，蓋國語長髯人也。

translations.literal: The emperor valued his words, kept him at his side, and thereafter called Chucai Uthu Sahalir rather than by name; Uthu Sahalir means in the national language "long-bearded man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor respected this answer, kept him close, and thereafter addressed him as Uthu Sahalir instead of by name—Mongolian for "the long-bearded man."

sentences.zh: 己卯夏六月，帝西討回回國。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the year jimao, the emperor campaigned west against the Muslim states.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in the jimao year, the emperor marched west against the Muslim kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 祃旗之日，雨雪三尺，帝疑之，楚材曰：「玄冥之氣，見於盛夏，克敵之徵也。

translations.literal: On the day of the war-banner rite, snow fell three chi deep; the emperor was doubtful, and Chucai said, "The qi of the Dark North appearing in midsummer is a sign of conquering the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: On the day the war banners were consecrated, snow piled three chi deep. When the emperor hesitated, Chucai said, "Yin force appearing in midsummer is a sign that the enemy will be overcome."

sentences.zh: 」庚辰冬，大雷，復問之，對曰：「回回國主當死於野。

translations.literal: In the winter of the year gengchen there was a great thunderclap; the emperor asked again, and he replied, "The ruler of the Muslim states will die in the wild."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the gengchen year there was a great thunderclap. Asked again, Chucai said, "The Muslim king will die in the open country."

sentences.zh: 」後皆驗。

translations.literal: Later both were verified.
translations.idiomatic: Both predictions later came true.

sentences.zh: 夏人常八斤，以善造弓見知於帝，因每自矜曰：「國家方用武，耶律儒者何用。

translations.literal: The Xia man Chang Bajin, known to the emperor for skill in making bows, would boast, "The state is now employing force—of what use is the Khitan scholar?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang Bajin, a man of Xia famed for bow-making, often boasted before the emperor, "The realm is at war—what use is a Khitan scholar?"

sentences.zh: 」楚材曰：「治弓尚須用弓匠，為天下者豈可不用治天下匠耶？

translations.literal: Chucai said, "Even in making bows one still needs a bow-maker—how can one who holds the realm under heaven do without craftsmen who govern the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai replied, "Even bow-making needs a bow-maker. How can the ruler of all under heaven do without craftsmen who know how to govern?"

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之甚喜，日見親用。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this with great delight and daily drew him closer in trust.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and relied on him more closely every day.

sentences.zh: 西域歷人奏五月望夜月當蝕，楚材曰：「否。

translations.literal: A Western Regions calendar master reported that the moon would eclipse on the night of the fifteenth of the fifth month; Chucai said, "No."
translations.idiomatic: A calendar master from the Western Regions said the moon would eclipse on the night of the fifth-month full moon. Chucai said it would not.

sentences.zh: 」卒不蝕。

translations.literal: In the end there was no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: No eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，楚材言月當蝕，西域人曰不蝕，至期果蝕八分。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year Chucai said the moon would eclipse; the Westerners said it would not; when the day came, it indeed eclipsed eight-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the tenth month, Chucai predicted an eclipse while the Westerners denied it; on the appointed day the moon was indeed eclipsed eight-tenths.

sentences.zh: 壬午八月，長星見西方，楚材曰：「女直將易主矣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the year renwu a long-tailed comet appeared in the west; Chucai said, "The Jurchen will soon change rulers."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the renwu year a comet with a long tail appeared in the west. Chucai said, "The Jurchen throne is about to change hands."

sentences.zh: 」明年，金宣宗果死。

translations.literal: The next year Jin Emperor Xuanzong indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jin Emperor Xuanzong did in fact die.

sentences.zh: 帝每征討，必命楚材卜，帝亦自灼羊胛，以相符應。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor campaigned, he always ordered Chucai to divine; the emperor also scorched sheep shoulder-blades himself to compare the results.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign the emperor had Chucai cast auguries, while he himself scorched sheep shoulder-blades to see whether the signs agreed.

sentences.zh: 指楚材謂太宗曰：「此人天賜我家。

translations.literal: Pointing to Chucai he said to Taizong, "This man Heaven has bestowed on our house."
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to Chucai and told Taizong, "Heaven has given this man to our house."

sentences.zh: 爾後軍國庶政，當悉委之。

translations.literal: Hereafter in military and civil affairs of every sort you should entrust everything to him."
translations.idiomatic: After I am gone, you should entrust all military and civil affairs to him."

sentences.zh: 」甲申，帝至東印度，駐鐵門關，有一角獸，形如鹿而馬尾，其色綠，作人言，謂侍衛者曰：「汝主宜早還。

translations.literal: In the year jiashen the emperor reached eastern India and halted at Iron Gate Pass; there was a horned beast shaped like a deer but with a horse's tail, green in color, that spoke in human language to the guards, saying, "Your lord should return soon."
translations.idiomatic: In the jiashen year the emperor reached eastern India and camped at Iron Gate Pass. A horned beast shaped like a deer with a horse's tail and green in color spoke to the guards in human language: "Your lord should return soon."

sentences.zh: 」帝以問楚材，對曰：「此瑞獸也，其名角端，能言四方語，好生惡殺，此天降符以告陛下。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Chucai, who replied, "This is an auspicious beast; its name is Jiaoduan. It can speak the languages of the four quarters, loves life and hates killing—this is a sign sent down from Heaven to inform Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Chucai, who answered, "This is an auspicious beast called Jiaoduan. It speaks the languages of the four quarters, loves life and hates slaughter. Heaven has sent this sign to warn Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 陛下天之元子，天下之人，皆陛下之子，願承天心，以全民命。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is Heaven's eldest son; all the people under heaven are Your Majesty's children. I pray that you receive Heaven's mind and thereby preserve the lives of the people."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is Heaven's eldest son, and all people under heaven are your children. I beg you to heed Heaven's will and spare the lives of the people."

sentences.zh: 」帝即日班師。

translations.literal: That same day the emperor withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: That very day the emperor turned the army homeward.

sentences.zh: 丙戌冬，從下靈武，諸將爭取子女金帛，楚材獨收遺書及大黃藥材。

translations.literal: In the winter of the year bingxu, following the reduction of Lingwu, the generals vied for women, children, gold, and silk; Chucai alone collected lost books and rhubarb medicinal materials.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the bingxu year, after the fall of Lingwu, the generals scrambled for women, children, gold, and silk while Chucai alone gathered abandoned books and stores of rhubarb.

sentences.zh: 既而士卒病疫，得大黃輒愈。

translations.literal: Before long the soldiers fell ill with epidemic disease; those who obtained rhubarb were promptly cured.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the troops fell sick with plague, and those who received rhubarb recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 帝自經營西土，未暇定制，州郡長吏，生殺任情，至孥人妻女，取貨財，兼土田。

translations.literal: Since the emperor had been occupied with the western territories and had not yet had leisure to establish regulations, prefectural and district chief officials killed or spared at will, even seizing men's wives and daughters, taking goods and wealth, and annexing fields and land.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was still securing the western territories he had no time to set laws in place. Prefectural officials killed or spared as they pleased, seized wives and daughters, plundered goods, and seized fields at will.

sentences.zh: 燕薊留後長官石抹咸得卜尤貪暴，殺人盈市。

translations.literal: Shimo Xiandebi, chief official and acting commander of Yan and Ji, was especially greedy and violent; killings filled the marketplaces.
translations.idiomatic: Shimo Xiandebi, the acting commander of Yan and Ji, was especially greedy and brutal; corpses filled the markets.

sentences.zh: 楚材聞之泣下，即入奏，請禁州郡，非奉璽書，不得擅徵發，囚當大辟者必待報，違者罪死，於是貪暴之風稍戢。

translations.literal: When Chucai heard this he wept and at once entered to memorialize, requesting that prefectures and districts be forbidden to levy or dispatch troops without an imperial edict bearing the seal, and that prisoners liable to capital punishment must await report before execution—violators to be punished by death; thereby the wind of greed and violence was somewhat checked.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai wept when he heard of it and immediately memorialized the throne. No prefecture might levy troops or execute capital sentences without an imperial sealed order; violators were to die. The worst abuses began to subside.

sentences.zh: 燕多劇賊，未夕，輒曳牛車指富家，取其財物，不與則殺之。

translations.literal: Yan had many fierce bandits who, before evening, would drag ox-carts to wealthy households, seize their goods, and kill them if they did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yan swarmed with violent robbers who, before nightfall, would drive ox-carts to rich houses, seize their goods, and kill anyone who resisted.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗以皇子監國，事聞，遣中使偕楚材往窮治之。

translations.literal: At the time Ruizong was regent as imperial prince; when the matter was reported, he sent a palace envoy together with Chucai to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ruizong was then regent. When the case came to his attention he sent a palace envoy with Chucai to investigate to the end.

sentences.zh: 楚材詢察得其姓名，皆留後親屬及勢家子，盡捕下獄。

translations.literal: Chucai inquired and ascertained their names; all were relatives of the acting commander and sons of powerful families; he arrested them all and imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai traced the culprits and found them all to be relatives of the acting commander or sons of powerful families. He had every one of them arrested.

sentences.zh: 其家賂中使，將緩之，楚材示以禍福，中使懼，從其言，獄具，戮十六人於市，燕民始安。

translations.literal: Their families bribed the palace envoy, who was about to relax the case; Chucai showed him the consequences of fortune and misfortune; the envoy feared and followed his counsel; when the case was concluded sixteen were executed in the market, and the people of Yan were at last at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Their families bribed the palace envoy, who was ready to soften the case. Chucai showed him what fortune and ruin would follow. The envoy took fright, followed Chucai's advice, and when the trial ended sixteen men were executed in the market. Only then did the people of Yan feel safe.

sentences.zh: 中原甫定，民多誤觸禁網，而國法無赦令。

translations.literal: The Central Plains had just been pacified; the people often unwittingly violated prohibitions, yet the national law had no amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains had only just been secured, and many people stumbled into the penal code by mistake, yet the state law allowed no general pardon.

sentences.zh: 楚材議請肆宥，眾以為迂，楚材獨從容為帝言。

translations.literal: Chucai proposed requesting a general pardon; the multitude thought this impractical, but Chucai alone spoke to the emperor at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai urged a general amnesty. Others called the idea impractical, but Chucai alone spoke to the emperor calmly and at length.

sentences.zh: 詔自庚寅正月朔日前事勿治。

translations.literal: An edict declared that offenses before the first day of the first month of the year gengyin were not to be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that crimes committed before the first day of the first month of the gengyin year would not be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 且條便宜一十八事頒天下，其略言：「郡宜置長吏牧民，設萬戶總軍，使勢均力敵，以遏驕橫。

translations.literal: He also set forth eighteen expedient measures to be promulgated throughout the realm, in summary saying: "Each commandery should appoint a chief official to shepherd the people and establish ten-thousand-household commanders to oversee the army, so that power is evenly matched and arrogance checked."
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted eighteen administrative measures for promulgation nationwide. In brief they held that each commandery should have a civil magistrate to govern the people and a ten-thousand-household commander for military affairs, with their powers balanced so that arrogance could be checked.

sentences.zh: 中原之地，財用所出，宜存卹其民，州縣非奉上命，敢擅行科差者罪之。

translations.literal: The Central Plains are where revenue is produced; the people should be preserved and comforted. Prefectures and districts that dare levy exactions without imperial command are to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains are the source of state revenue; the people there must be protected. Any prefecture or district that levies exactions without imperial command is to be punished.

sentences.zh: 貿易借貸官物者罪之。

translations.literal: Those who trade in or borrow government goods on loan are to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Trading in or borrowing government property on loan is to be punished.

sentences.zh: 蒙古、回鶻、河西諸人，種地不納稅者死。

translations.literal: Mongols, Uighurs, and people of the Hexi region who cultivate land but do not pay taxes are to die.
translations.idiomatic: Any Mongol, Uighur, or Hexi cultivator who farms land but refuses taxes is to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 監主自盜官物者死。

translations.literal: Supervisors who steal government goods themselves are to die.
translations.idiomatic: Any supervisor who steals government property is to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 應犯死罪者，具由申奏待報，然後行刑。

translations.literal: Those liable to capital punishment must set forth the grounds, memorialize and await report, and only then be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Capital cases must be reported in full to the throne and may be carried out only after imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 貢獻禮物，為害非輕，深宜禁斷。

translations.literal: Presenting tribute-gifts does harm that is no small matter and should be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The custom of presenting tribute-gifts does grave harm and ought to be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 」帝悉從之，唯貢獻一事不允，曰：「彼自願饋獻者，宜聽之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented to all, save only the matter of tribute-gifts, which he did not approve, saying, "Those who wish of their own accord to present gifts should be allowed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted everything except the ban on tribute-gifts. "If people wish to offer gifts of their own accord," he said, "they should be allowed."

sentences.zh: 」楚材曰：「蠹害之端，必由於此。

translations.literal: Chucai said, "The beginning of ruinous harm must come from this."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "This is where corruption always begins."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「凡卿所奏，無不從者，卿不能從朕一事耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "In all you have memorialized there is nothing I have not followed—can you not follow me in this one matter?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have agreed to everything you proposed. Can you not yield to me on this one point?"

sentences.zh: 太祖之世，歲有事西域，未暇經理中原，官吏多聚斂自私，貲至巨萬，而官無儲彳侍。

translations.literal: In Taizu's time there were campaigns in the Western Regions every year; there was no leisure to administer the Central Plains. Officials mostly extorted for themselves until their wealth reached tens of millions, while the government had no stored supplies ready for use.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Taizu's reign yearly campaigns in the west left no time to govern the Central Plains. Officials enriched themselves until their private fortunes reached millions, while the treasury had nothing in reserve.

sentences.zh: 近臣別迭等言：「漢人無補於國，可悉空其人以為牧地。

translations.literal: The close minister Biedie and others said, "The Han people are of no benefit to the state; we can empty them all out and make the land pasture."
translations.idiomatic: The intimate adviser Biedie and others said, "The Han are useless to the state. Drive them all out and turn the land into pasture."

sentences.zh: 」楚材曰：「陛下將南伐，軍需宜有所資，誠均定中原地稅、商稅、鹽、酒、鐵冶、山澤之利，歲可得銀五十萬兩、帛八萬匹、粟四十餘萬石，足以供給，何謂無補哉？

translations.literal: Chucai said, "Your Majesty is about to campaign south; military supplies ought to have a source. If we truly equalize and fix land tax, commercial tax, and the profits of salt, wine, iron smelting, and mountain and marsh resources in the Central Plains, each year we can obtain five hundred thousand taels of silver, eighty thousand bolts of silk, and more than four hundred thousand shi of grain—enough to supply needs. How can you say they are of no benefit?"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "Your Majesty is about to march south and will need supplies. If we regularize land tax, commercial tax, and revenues from salt, wine, ironworks, and mountain and marsh monopolies in the Central Plains, the state can draw five hundred thousand taels of silver, eighty thousand bolts of silk, and more than four hundred thousand shi of grain a year—enough for any campaign. How can the Han be called useless?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿試為朕行之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Try it for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then put the scheme into practice for me."

sentences.zh: 」乃奏立燕京等十路徵收課稅使，凡長貳悉用士人，如陳時可、趙昉等，皆寬厚長者，極天下之選，參佐皆用省部舊人。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized to establish tax-collection commissioners for ten circuits including Yanjing; all chief and deputy posts were filled with scholar-officials such as Chen Shike and Zhao Fang, all men of generous character and mature years, the finest selection in the realm; assistants were all drawn from former personnel of the ministries and departments.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to establish tax commissioners for ten circuits including Yanjing. Every chief and deputy post went to scholar-officials such as Chen Shike and Zhao Fang—men of generous and seasoned character, the best the realm could offer—with assistants drawn from former central-government staff.

sentences.zh: 辛卯秋，帝至雲中，十路咸進廩籍及金帛陳於廷中，帝笑謂楚材曰：「汝不去朕左右，而能使國用充足，南國之臣，復有如卿者乎？

translations.literal: In the autumn of the year xinmao the emperor reached Yunzhong; all ten circuits presented granary registers and gold and silk displayed in the court hall. The emperor smiled and said to Chucai, "You do not leave my side, yet you can make state revenue ample—among the ministers of the southern states, is there another like you?"
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the xinmao year the emperor reached Yunzhong. All ten circuits presented granary registers together with gold and silk laid out in the hall. The emperor smiled at Chucai and said, "You never leave my side, yet you have filled the treasury. Are there any ministers in the southern states who can match you?"

sentences.zh: 「對曰：「在彼者皆賢於臣，臣不才，故留燕，為陛下用。

translations.literal: He replied, "Those there are all more worthy than I; I am without talent, and therefore remained in Yan to serve Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai answered, "The men in the south are all more capable than I. I lacked talent, so I stayed in Yan to serve Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其謙，賜之酒。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his modesty and bestowed wine on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his modesty and rewarded him with wine.

sentences.zh: 即日拜中書令，事無鉅細，皆先白之。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed Director of the Secretariat; in affairs great or small, all were first reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was appointed director of the secretariat, and every matter, great or small, was referred to him first.

sentences.zh: 楚材奏：「凡州郡宜令長吏專理民事，萬戶總軍政，凡所掌課稅，權貴不得侵之。

translations.literal: Chucai memorialized: "In every prefecture and district the chief official should be ordered to administer civil affairs exclusively, while the ten-thousand-household commander oversees military affairs; all tax revenues under their charge may not be encroached upon by the powerful and noble."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai memorialized that in every prefecture the civil magistrate should handle civilian affairs alone, the ten-thousand-household commander military affairs alone, and that no powerful noble might seize the taxes under their charge.

sentences.zh: 」又舉鎮海、粘合，均與之同事，權貴不能平。

translations.literal: He also recommended Zhenhai and Nianhe to share office with him equally; the powerful and noble could not be reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Zhenhai and Nianhe to share power with him on equal footing, which the great families could not accept.

sentences.zh: 咸得卜以舊怨，尤疾之，譖於宗王曰：「耶律中書令率用親舊，必有二心，宜奏殺之。

translations.literal: Xiandebi, because of an old grudge, especially hated him and slandered him to a prince of the blood, saying, "The Khitan Director of the Secretariat chiefly employs kin and old associates and must harbor divided loyalty; he should be memorialized for execution."
translations.idiomatic: Xiandebi, nursing an old grudge, hated him all the more and told a imperial prince, "The Khitan director of the secretariat fills his office with kin and friends. He must be disloyal. Memorializing for his death would be right."

sentences.zh: 」宗王遣使以聞，帝察其誣，責使者，罷遣之。

translations.literal: The prince sent an envoy to report; the emperor perceived the false accusation, reproved the envoy, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent an envoy to report this. The emperor saw the slander for what it was, rebuked the envoy, and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 屬有訟咸得卜不法者，帝命楚材鞫之，奏曰：「此人倨傲，故易招謗。

translations.literal: When there came a suit against Xiandebi for unlawful conduct, the emperor ordered Chucai to try him; he memorialized, "This man is arrogant and therefore easily draws slander."
translations.idiomatic: When a case was brought against Xiandebi for misconduct, the emperor ordered Chucai to try him. Chucai reported, "This man is arrogant and therefore invites slander."

sentences.zh: 今將有事南方，他日治之未晚也。

translations.literal: We are now about to have business in the south; to deal with him another day would not be late."
translations.idiomatic: We are about to campaign in the south. Punishing him can wait until another day."

sentences.zh: 」帝私謂侍臣曰：「楚材不較私仇，真寬厚長者，汝曹當效之。

translations.literal: The emperor privately told his attendants, "Chucai does not settle private scores—truly a generous and mature man; you should emulate him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants privately, "Chucai will not pursue a private grudge. He is truly a generous and mature man. You should take him as your model."

sentences.zh: 」中貴可思不花奏採金銀役夫及種田西域與栽蒲萄戶，帝令於西京宣德徙萬餘戶充之。

translations.literal: The palace favorite Kesibuhua memorialized to recruit laborers for mining gold and silver and to plant fields in the Western Regions and households to cultivate grapes; the emperor ordered more than ten thousand households moved from Xijing and Xuande to fill the need.
translations.idiomatic: The palace favorite Kesibuhua asked for laborers to mine gold and silver, farm the Western Regions, and plant vineyards. The emperor ordered more than ten thousand households moved from Xijing and Xuande to supply them.

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「先帝遺詔，山後民質樸，無異國人，緩急可用，不宜輕動。

translations.literal: Chucai said, "The late emperor's testamentary edict said that the people behind the mountains are simple and honest, no different from our own people, usable in urgent or easy times—they should not be lightly moved."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "The late emperor's testament warned that the people north of the Yan range are plain and loyal, no different from our own folk, and useful in any emergency. They should not be uprooted lightly."

sentences.zh: 今將徵河南，請無殘民以給此役。

translations.literal: We are now about to campaign against Henan; I beg that the people not be ravaged to supply this labor."
translations.idiomatic: We are about to conquer Henan. I beg you not to ruin these people to supply this project."

sentences.zh: 」帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 壬辰春，帝南征，將涉河，詔逃難之民，來降者免死。

translations.literal: In the spring of the year renchen the emperor campaigned south; about to cross the river, he decreed that refugees who came to surrender would be spared death.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the renchen year the emperor marched south. Before crossing the river he decreed that refugees who surrendered would be spared.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「此輩急則降，緩則走，徒以資敵，不可宥。

translations.literal: Some said, "These people surrender when pressed and flee when relaxed, merely supplying the enemy—they cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Some argued, "They surrender when pressed and flee when the danger passes. They only feed the enemy and ought not to be spared."

sentences.zh: 」楚材請制旗數百，以給降民，使歸田裡，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Chucai requested that several hundred banners be made to give to the surrendered people, enabling them to return to their villages; very many lives were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai asked for several hundred safe-conduct banners for the surrendered people so they could return home. A great multitude was thus saved.

sentences.zh: 舊制，凡攻城邑，敵以矢石相加者，即為拒命，既克，必殺之。

translations.literal: By old regulation, whenever a walled city was attacked, if the enemy exchanged arrows and stones, that counted as defiance; once taken, all were invariably killed.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom any city that resisted with arrows and stones was treated as defiant, and once captured its people were always put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 汴梁將下，大將速不台遣使來言：「金人抗拒持久，師多死傷，城下之日，宜屠之。

translations.literal: As Bianliang was about to fall, the great general Subutai sent a messenger saying, "The Jin resisted for a long time and many in the army were killed or wounded; on the day the city falls, it should be put to the sword."
translations.idiomatic: As Bianliang was about to fall, Subutai sent word: "The Jin held out so long that our army suffered heavily. When the city falls it should be slaughtered."

sentences.zh: 」楚材馳入奏曰：「將士暴露數十年，所欲者土地人民耳。

translations.literal: Chucai galloped in to memorialize, "The officers and soldiers have been exposed to the elements for decades; what they desire is land and people."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai rode in at once and said, "Your soldiers have campaigned in the open for decades. What they want is land and people."

sentences.zh: 得地無民，將焉用之！

translations.literal: If you gain the land without the people, of what use will it be!
translations.idiomatic: What use is land without people?"

sentences.zh: 」帝猶豫未決，楚材曰：「奇巧之工，厚藏之家，皆萃於此，若盡殺之，將無所獲。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and had not decided; Chucai said, "Skilled artisans of rare craft and families of deep wealth are all gathered here—if you kill them all, you will gain nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still hesitated. Chucai said, "The finest craftsmen and the wealthiest households in the realm are all here. If you kill everyone you will gain nothing."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，詔罪止完顏氏，餘皆勿問。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed; an edict declared that guilt extended only to the Wanyan clan, and the rest were not to be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and decreed that only the Wanyan clan would be punished; all others were to go unharmed.

sentences.zh: 時避兵居汴者得百四十七萬人。

translations.literal: At the time those sheltering from war in Bian numbered 1,470,000 persons.
translations.idiomatic: At that time 1,470,000 people who had taken refuge in Bian were spared.

sentences.zh: 楚材又請遣人入城，求孔子後，得五十一代孫元措，奏襲封衍聖公，付以林廟地。

translations.literal: Chucai also requested that someone be sent into the city to seek a descendant of Confucius; they obtained Yuan Cuo, fifty-first-generation descendant, memorialized to inherit the title Duke Yansheng, and entrusted with the forest temple lands.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai also sent men into the city to find a descendant of Confucius. They found Yuan Cuo, fifty-first in line, and memorialized that he inherit the title Duke Yansheng together with the temple estates.

sentences.zh: 命收太常禮樂生，及召名儒梁陟、王萬慶、趙著等，使直釋九經，進講東宮。

translations.literal: He ordered the collection of ritual-music students of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and summoned eminent Confucians Liang Zhi, Wang Wanqing, Zhao Zhu, and others, assigning them to interpret the Nine Classics and lecture before the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered students of ritual music from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and summoned eminent scholars such as Liang Zhi, Wang Wanqing, and Zhao Zhu to annotate the Nine Classics and lecture in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 又率大臣子孫，執經解義，俾知聖人之道。

translations.literal: He also led the sons and grandsons of great ministers to hold the classics and explain their meaning, so that they might know the Way of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the sons and grandsons of high ministers study the classics and expound their meaning so they might learn the way of the sages.

sentences.zh: 置編修所於燕京、經籍所於平陽，由是文治興焉。

translations.literal: He established a compilation office at Yanjing and a classics repository at Pingyang; from this literary governance arose.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a compilation office in Yanjing and a classics repository in Pingyang, and from that point civil culture began to flourish.

sentences.zh: 時河南初破，俘獲甚眾，軍還，逃者十七八。

translations.literal: At the time Henan had just been broken; captives were very numerous, but when the army returned, seven or eight in ten had fled.
translations.idiomatic: Henan had just fallen and captives were numerous, yet when the army marched home seven or eight in ten had escaped.

sentences.zh: 有旨：居停逃民及資給者，滅其家，鄉社亦連坐。

translations.literal: There was an order that those who harbored fugitives or supplied them should have their families exterminated, and village communities were also implicated by collective punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An order went out that anyone who sheltered fugitives or aided them would have his household destroyed, and the local community would be punished as well.

sentences.zh: 由是逃者莫敢舍，多殍死道路。

translations.literal: Because of this the fugitives dared accept no shelter, and many starved to death on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives dared accept no shelter, and many starved or died along the roads.

sentences.zh: 楚材從容進曰：「河南既平，民皆陛下赤子，走復何之！

translations.literal: Chucai calmly advanced and said, "Henan is already pacified; the people are all Your Majesty's infants—where can they flee!"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai spoke calmly: "Henan is already pacified. These people are all your children. Where else can they run?"

sentences.zh: 奈何因一俘囚，連死數十百人乎？

translations.literal: How can you, because of one captive, link to death dozens or hundreds of people?
translations.idiomatic: Why should one escaped captive bring death to dozens or hundreds?"

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，命除其禁。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and ordered the prohibition removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the point and revoked the order.

sentences.zh: 金之亡也，唯秦、鞏二十餘州久未下，楚材奏曰：「往年吾民逃罪，或萃於此，故以死拒戰，若許以不殺，將不攻自下矣。

translations.literal: In the fall of Jin, only more than twenty prefectures including Qin and Gong long remained untaken; Chucai memorialized, "In former years our people fled crimes and gathered here, and therefore fought to the death; if you promise not to kill, they will surrender without attack."
translations.idiomatic: As Jin was collapsing, more than twenty prefectures including Qin and Gong still held out. Chucai said, "In past years fugitives from our side gathered there and fought to the death because they feared slaughter. Promise them their lives and the cities will surrender without a fight."

sentences.zh: 」詔下，諸城皆降。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, all the cities surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict went out, every city submitted.

sentences.zh: 甲午，議籍中原民，大臣忽都虎等議，以丁為戶。

translations.literal: In the year jiawu, when registering the people of the Central Plains was discussed, the great minister Huduhu and others proposed taking adult males as the household unit.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year, when the court debated registering the people of the Central Plains, Huduhu and other ministers proposed using adult males as the unit of taxation.

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Chucai said, "That will not do."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "That cannot be allowed."

sentences.zh: 丁逃，則賦無所出，當以戶定之。

translations.literal: If adult males flee, then tax revenue will have no source; households should be the unit.
translations.idiomatic: If you count only adult males, they will flee and revenue will vanish. Taxation must be based on households.

sentences.zh: 」爭之再三，卒以戶定。

translations.literal: He argued repeatedly, and in the end household registration was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He argued the point again and again until the court finally adopted the household unit.

sentences.zh: 時將相大臣有所驅獲，往往寄留諸郡，楚材因括戶口，並令為民，匿佔者死。

translations.literal: At the time generals, ministers, and great officials who had seized people often left them in various commanderies; Chucai therefore conducted a household census, ordered them all registered as common people, and made concealment or seizure punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and ministers often kept captives in various prefectures. Chucai ordered a census, registered them all as subjects, and decreed death for anyone who hid or seized people illegally.

sentences.zh: 乙未，朝議將四征不廷，若遣回回人徵江南，漢人征西域，深得制御之術，楚材曰：「不可。

translations.literal: In the year yiwei the court discussed campaigning against the four powers that had not submitted; some proposed sending Muslims to conquer the Jiangnan and Han people to campaign in the Western Regions, saying this was a profound method of control. Chucai said, "That will not do."
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year the court debated campaigns against unsubmissive states. Some proposed sending Muslims against the Jiangnan and Han troops against the west, calling this a master stroke of control. Chucai said it would not work.

sentences.zh: 中原、西域，相去遼遠，未至敵境，人馬疲乏，兼水土異宜，疾疫將生，宜各從其便。

translations.literal: The Central Plains and the Western Regions are vastly distant from each other; before reaching enemy territory men and horses are exhausted, and moreover water and soil differ in suitability—plague will arise. Each side should act as suits it best."
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains and the Western Regions are immensely far apart. Troops would be exhausted before reaching the enemy, and different climates would breed plague. Each army should fight in its own region."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙申春，諸王大集，帝親執觴賜楚材曰：「朕之所以推誠任卿者，先帝之命也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the year bingshen the princes gathered in great numbers; the emperor personally raised a cup and bestowed it on Chucai, saying, "The reason I trust you with all sincerity is the late emperor's command."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the bingshen year the princes assembled. The emperor personally raised a cup for Chucai and said, "I place my full trust in you because the late emperor commanded it."

sentences.zh: 非卿，則中原無今日。

translations.literal: Without you, the Central Plains would not have today.
translations.idiomatic: Without you the Central Plains would not be what they are today.

sentences.zh: 朕所以得安枕者，卿之力也。

translations.literal: That I can sleep at ease is your strength.
translations.idiomatic: It is through your efforts that I can sleep in peace.

sentences.zh: 」西域諸國及宋、高麗使者來朝，語多不實，帝指楚材示之曰：「汝國有如此人乎？

translations.literal: Envoys from the Western Regions states, Song, and Goryeo came to court; their words were mostly untrue. The emperor pointed to Chucai and showed him to them, saying, "Does your state have anyone like this?"
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from the Western Regions, Song, and Goryeo came to court with speeches full of flattery. The emperor pointed to Chucai and asked, "Does your country have anyone like him?"

sentences.zh: 」皆謝曰：「無有。

translations.literal: They all apologized and said, "There is not."
translations.idiomatic: They all bowed and said there was not.

sentences.zh: 殆神人也。

translations.literal: He is nearly a divine man.
translations.idiomatic: He is almost more than human.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「汝等唯此言不妄，朕亦度必無此人。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "In this alone your words are not false; I too judge that your states surely have no such man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That alone you speak truly. I too am sure your countries have no such man."

sentences.zh: 」有於元者，奏行交鈔，楚材曰：「金章宗時初行交鈔，與錢通行，有司以出鈔為利，收鈔為諱，謂之老鈔，至以萬貫唯易一餅。

translations.literal: Someone at court memorialized to issue paper notes; Chucai said, "Under Jin Emperor Zhangzong paper notes were first issued and circulated with coin; the offices took issuing notes as profit and receiving them as taboo, calling them old notes, until ten thousand strings could buy only one cake."
translations.idiomatic: Someone at court proposed issuing paper currency. Chucai said, "Jin introduced paper notes under Emperor Zhangzong. Officials profited by printing notes and refused to redeem them, calling them stale notes, until ten thousand strings bought only a single cake."

sentences.zh: 民力困竭，國用匱乏，當為鑑戒。

translations.literal: The people's strength was exhausted and state revenue depleted—this should serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The people were exhausted and the treasury empty. That history should be our warning.

sentences.zh: 今印造交鈔，宜不過萬錠。

translations.literal: If we now print paper notes, the issue should not exceed ten thousand ingots.
translations.idiomatic: If notes are printed now, the issue should not exceed ten thousand ingots.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，忽都虎以民籍至，帝議裂州縣賜親王功臣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Huduhu arrived with the household registers; the emperor discussed carving up prefectures and districts to bestow on imperial princes and meritorious officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Huduhu delivered the household registers. The emperor discussed dividing prefectures among princes and meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「裂土分民，易生嫌隙，不如多以金帛與之。

translations.literal: Chucai said, "Splitting land and dividing the people easily breeds suspicion and rifts; it would be better to give them more gold and silk."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "Dividing land and people breeds suspicion. It would be better to reward them with gold and silk."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「已許奈何？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "It has already been promised—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have already promised. What can be done now?"

sentences.zh: 」楚材曰：「若朝廷置吏，收其貢賦，歲終頒之，使毋擅科徵，可也。

translations.literal: Chucai said, "If the court appoints officials to collect their tribute and taxes and distributes them at year's end, forbidding unauthorized levies, that will do."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "Let the court appoint officials to collect the taxes and distribute them at year's end, so the princes cannot levy on their own. That will suffice."

sentences.zh: 」帝然其計，遂定天下賦稅，每二戶出絲一斤，以給國用；

translations.literal: The emperor approved his plan and thereupon fixed taxes for the realm: every two households were to contribute one jin of silk for state use;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and fixed taxes for the realm: every two households owed one jin of silk for state revenue;

sentences.zh: 五戶出絲一斤，以給諸王功臣湯沐之資。

translations.literal: every five households one jin of silk for the bath-fief funds of the princes and meritorious officials.
translations.idiomatic: and every five households one jin of silk for the princes' and meritorious officials' maintenance allotments.

sentences.zh: 地稅，中田每畝二升又半，上田三升，下田二升，水田每畝五升；

translations.literal: Land tax: medium fields two and a half sheng per mu, upper fields three sheng, lower fields two sheng, paddy fields five sheng per mu;
translations.idiomatic: Land tax was set at two and a half sheng per mu for medium fields, three for upper fields, two for lower fields, and five for paddy;

sentences.zh: 商稅，三十分而一；

translations.literal: commercial tax, one part in thirty;
translations.idiomatic: commercial tax at one-thirtieth;

sentences.zh: 鹽價，銀一兩四十斤。

translations.literal: salt price, one tael of silver for forty jin.
translations.idiomatic: and salt at forty jin per tael of silver.

sentences.zh: 既定常賦，朝議以為太輕，楚材曰：「作法於涼，其弊猶貪，後將有以利進者，則今已重矣。

translations.literal: Once the regular levies were fixed, the court discussed them as too light; Chucai said, "If one makes law in lenient times, its abuse is still greed; when later men advance proposals for profit, what is light today will already be heavy."
translations.idiomatic: When the regular taxes were fixed, the court called them too light. Chucai said, "Even lenient laws breed greed. When later men press for profit, today's light burden will already seem heavy."

sentences.zh: 」時工匠製造，糜費官物，十私八九，楚材請皆考核之，以為定制。

translations.literal: At the time craftsmen in manufacture wasted government goods, eight or nine in ten for private use; Chucai requested that all be audited and made a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen were wasting government materials, keeping eight or nine parts in ten for themselves. Chucai ordered audits and made fixed regulations.

sentences.zh: 時侍臣脫歡奏簡天下室女，詔下，楚材尼之不行，帝怒。

translations.literal: At the time the attendant minister Tuohuan memorialized to select maidens throughout the realm; when the edict was issued Chucai blocked its execution and the emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant Tuohuan proposed selecting maidens empire-wide. When the edict was issued Chucai blocked it, and the emperor grew angry.

sentences.zh: 楚材進曰：「向擇美女二十有八人，足備使令。

translations.literal: Chucai advanced and said, "Previously twenty-eight beautiful women were chosen, enough to supply attendance."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "Twenty-eight women have already been chosen, enough for the palace."

sentences.zh: 今復選拔，臣恐擾民，欲覆奏耳。

translations.literal: To select again now, I fear disturbing the people—I wished only to report back for reconsideration.
translations.idiomatic: Another selection would trouble the people. I only wished to report back for reconsideration.

sentences.zh: 」帝良久曰：「可罷之。

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor said, "It may be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause the emperor said, "Let it be canceled."

sentences.zh: 」又欲收民牝馬，楚材曰：「田蠶之地，非馬所產，今若行之，後必為人害。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to seize the people's brood mares; Chucai said, "This is land of fields and silkworms, not where horses are bred; if this is done now, later it will surely harm the people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wanted to seize the people's brood mares. Chucai said, "This is farming and sericulture country, not horse country. Do this now and later generations will suffer for it."

sentences.zh: 」又從之。

translations.literal: Again the emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Again the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，楚材奏曰：「制器者必用良工，守成者必用儒臣。

translations.literal: In the year dingyou Chucai memorialized, "Those who make implements must use skilled craftsmen; those who preserve an achievement must use Confucian ministers."
translations.idiomatic: In the dingyou year Chucai memorialized, "Making tools requires skilled craftsmen; preserving a realm requires Confucian ministers."

sentences.zh: 儒臣之事業，非積數十年，殆未易成也。

translations.literal: The enterprise of Confucian ministers is not accumulated in mere decades—it is scarcely easy to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Their work cannot be mastered in a few decades and is not easily done.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「果爾，可官其人。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If it is truly so, such men may be given office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If that is so, then give them office."

sentences.zh: 」楚材曰：「請校試之。

translations.literal: Chucai said, "I beg to examine and test them."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "Let them be examined first."

sentences.zh: 」乃命宣德州宣課使劉中隨郡考試，以經義、詞賦、論分為三科，儒人被俘為奴者，亦令就試，其主匿弗遣者死。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Liu Zhong, tax commissioner of Xuande Prefecture, to conduct examinations in each commandery, dividing into three categories: classical meaning, rhapsody, and discourse. Confucian scholars taken captive as slaves were also ordered to take the examination; masters who concealed them and did not send them were to die.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Liu Zhong, tax commissioner of Xuande, to examine candidates in each commandery in three fields: classical interpretation, rhapsody, and discourse. Captured scholars enslaved were also required to sit for the exam; masters who hid them were put to death.

sentences.zh: 得士凡四千三十人，免為奴者四之一。

translations.literal: Scholars obtained numbered 4,030 in all; one in four were freed from slavery.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand thirty scholars qualified, and one in four was freed from slavery.

sentences.zh: 先是，州郡長吏，多藉賈人銀以償官，息累數倍，曰羊羔兒利，至奴其妻子猶不足償。

translations.literal: Previously prefectural and district chief officials often borrowed merchants' silver to pay the government; interest accumulated to several times the principal, called "lamb-kid interest," until even enslaving their wives and children was insufficient to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural officials had often borrowed silver from merchants to meet government quotas. Interest multiplied several times over in what was called "lamb-kid interest," until even selling wives and children into slavery could not repay the debt.

sentences.zh: 楚材奏令本利相侔而止，永為定制，民間所負者，官為代價之。

translations.literal: Chucai memorialized that principal and interest should be made equal and then stopped, permanently as a fixed regulation; what the people owed, the government would pay on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai ordered that interest cease once it equaled principal, made the rule permanent, and had the government pay private debts on the people's behalf.

sentences.zh: 至一衡量，給符印，立鈔法，定均輸，布遞傳，明驛券，庶政略備，民稍蘇息焉。

translations.literal: Weights and measures were unified, seals and tallies issued, paper-note law established, equalized transport fixed, courier posts laid out, relay vouchers clarified—miscellaneous administration was largely complete, and the people gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: He standardized weights and measures, issued seals and tallies, established paper currency, regulated transport, set up courier posts, and clarified relay vouchers. Civil administration was largely in order, and the people began to recover.

sentences.zh: 有二道士爭長，互立黨與，其一誣其仇之黨二人為逃軍，結中貴及通事楊惟忠，執而虐殺之。

translations.literal: Two Daoist priests disputed for seniority and each formed factions; one falsely accused two men of his enemy's faction as deserters, joined with a palace favorite and the interpreter Yang Weizhong, seized them, and tortured them to death.
translations.idiomatic: Two Daoist priests vied for precedence and formed factions. One accused two members of his rival's faction of desertion, enlisted a palace favorite and the interpreter Yang Weizhong, seized the men, and tortured them to death.

sentences.zh: 楚材按收惟忠。

translations.literal: Chucai investigated and arrested Weizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai investigated and arrested Weizhong.

sentences.zh: 中貴复訴楚材違制，帝怒，系楚材；

translations.literal: The palace favorite again accused Chucai of violating regulations; the emperor was angry and imprisoned Chucai;
translations.idiomatic: The palace favorite accused Chucai of violating regulations. The emperor was furious and had Chucai bound;

sentences.zh: 既而自悔，命釋之。

translations.literal: before long he repented himself and ordered him released.
translations.idiomatic: but soon regretted it and ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 楚材不肯解縛，進曰：「臣備位公輔，國政所屬。

translations.literal: Chucai would not undo his bonds and advanced, saying, "I occupy the position of chief minister; state affairs depend on me."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai refused to be unbound and said, "I hold the highest ministerial office. The state's affairs depend on me."

sentences.zh: 陛下初令系臣，以有罪也，當明示百官，罪在不赦。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first ordered me bound, it was because I had guilt; you should clearly show the hundred officials that the crime was unpardonable.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first bound me, it was because I was guilty. You should announce to the officials that my crime was unpardonable.

sentences.zh: 今釋臣，是無罪也，豈宜輕易反覆，如戲小兒？

translations.literal: Now to release me is to say I am without guilt—how can one lightly go back and forth as if playing with a child?
translations.idiomatic: To release me now is to declare me innocent. How can the throne turn so lightly back and forth, as if playing with a child?

sentences.zh: 國有大事，何以行焉！

translations.literal: When the state has great affairs, how can they be carried out!
translations.idiomatic: How can great affairs of state be conducted this way!

sentences.zh: 」眾皆失色。

translations.literal: The assembly all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the hall turned pale.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕雖為帝，寧無過舉耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Though I am emperor, can I be without mistaken actions?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Even an emperor can err, can he not?"

sentences.zh: 」乃溫言以慰之。

translations.literal: He then spoke gently to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke gently to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 楚材因陳時務十策，曰：「信賞罰，正名分，給俸祿，官功臣，考殿最，均科差，選工匠，務農桑，定土貢，制漕運。

translations.literal: Chucai thereupon presented ten policies on current affairs, saying: "Trust in rewards and punishments, rectify names and ranks, grant salaries, appoint meritorious officials, examine performance, equalize levies, select craftsmen, devote effort to farming and sericulture, fix local tribute, and regulate grain transport by water."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai then presented ten policies on state affairs: trust rewards and punishments, rectify ranks, pay salaries, appoint meritorious men, examine performance, equalize levies, select craftsmen, promote farming and sericulture, fix local tribute, and regulate grain transport.

sentences.zh: 皆切於時務，悉施行之。

translations.literal: All were urgent to current affairs and were fully put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: All were urgently relevant, and all were put into practice.

sentences.zh: 太原路轉運使呂振、副使劉子振，以贓抵罪。

translations.literal: Lü Zhen, transport commissioner of Taiyuan Circuit, and Vice Commissioner Liu Zizhen were punished for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen, transport commissioner of Taiyuan, and his deputy Liu Zizhen were punished for corruption.

sentences.zh: 帝責楚材曰：「卿言孔子之教可行，儒者為好人，何故乃有此輩？

translations.literal: The emperor reproved Chucai, saying, "You said Confucius's teaching can be practiced and that Confucians are good men—why then are there men like these?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached Chucai: "You said Confucian teaching works and that scholars are good men. Why then do we have men like these?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「君父教臣子，亦不欲令陷不義。

translations.literal: He replied, "When lord and father teach their subjects and sons, they also do not wish them to fall into unrighteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai answered, "Even fathers and rulers do not wish their sons and subjects to fall into wrongdoing."

sentences.zh: 三綱五常，聖人之名教，有國家者莫不由之，如天之有日月也。

translations.literal: The Three Bonds and Five Constants are the sages' moral teaching; no state fails to follow them, as heaven has sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Bonds and Five Constants are the sages' moral teaching. No state can do without them, any more than heaven can do without sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 豈得緣一夫之失，使萬世常行之道獨見廢於我朝乎！

translations.literal: How can one, because of a single man's fault, let the Way practiced through ten thousand generations alone be abandoned in our dynasty!
translations.idiomatic: How can one man's failure justify abandoning in our dynasty alone the Way that all ages have followed!

sentences.zh: 」帝意乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was then eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 富人劉忽篤馬、涉獵發丁、劉廷玉等以銀一百四十萬兩撲買天下課稅，楚材曰：「此貪利之徒，罔上虐下，為害甚大。

translations.literal: The rich men Liu Huduma, Shelie Fading, Liu Tingyu, and others offered 1,400,000 taels of silver to monopolize purchase of taxes for the whole realm; Chucai said, "These are men greedy for profit who deceive superiors and abuse inferiors—the harm is very great."
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy Liu Huduma, Shelie Fading, Liu Tingyu, and others offered 1,400,000 taels to monopolize tax collection empire-wide. Chucai said, "These greedy men deceive the throne and abuse the people. The harm would be immense."

sentences.zh: 」奏罷之。

translations.literal: He memorialized and had it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized and had the scheme stopped.

sentences.zh: 常曰： 「興一利不如除一害，生一事不如省一事。

translations.literal: He often said: "To create one benefit is not as good as removing one harm; to generate one affair is not as good as eliminating one affair."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Creating one benefit is not as good as removing one harm; adding one task is not as good as cutting one task."

sentences.zh: 任尚以班超之言為平平耳，千古之下，自有定論。

translations.literal: Ren Shang took Ban Chao's words as merely ordinary; after a thousand years there will naturally be a settled judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shang thought Ban Chao's words merely ordinary, but after a thousand years history will judge them clearly.

sentences.zh: 後之負譴者，方知吾言之不妄也。

translations.literal: Men of later times who bear reproach will then know that my words were not false.
translations.idiomatic: Later men who suffer for their warnings will know I spoke no falsehood.

sentences.zh: 」帝素嗜酒，日與大臣酣飲，楚材屢諫，不聽，乃持酒槽鐵口進曰：「曲蘗能腐物，鐵尚如此，況五臟乎！

translations.literal: The emperor had always loved wine and daily drank deeply with his ministers; Chucai repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded, and therefore brought in the iron mouth of a wine vat and advanced, saying, "Yeast can rot things—even iron is thus, how much more the five viscera!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved wine and drank heavily with his ministers every day. Chucai remonstrated repeatedly without success, then brought in the iron mouth of a wine vat and said, "Ferment can rot even iron. How much more the organs of the body!"

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，語近臣曰： 「汝曹愛君憂國之心，豈有如吾圖撒合裡者耶？

translations.literal: The emperor understood and told his close attendants, "In mind of loving the ruler and worrying for the state, is there anyone like our Uthu Sahalir?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and told his attendants, "Who among you loves his ruler and cares for the state as Uthu Sahalir does?"

sentences.zh: 」賞以金帛，敕近臣日進酒三鐘而止。

translations.literal: He rewarded him with gold and silk and ordered close attendants to bring wine daily, stopping at three cups.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with gold and silk and ordered his attendants to limit his daily wine to three cups.

sentences.zh: 自庚寅定課稅格，至甲午平河南，歲有增羨，至戊戌，課銀增至一百一十萬兩。

translations.literal: From the gengyin year when the tax scale was fixed until the jiawu year when Henan was pacified, revenue increased yearly; by the wuxu year tax silver had risen to 1,100,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: From the gengyin year when tax rates were fixed until Henan was pacified in the jiawu year, revenue rose yearly. By the wuxu year tax silver reached 1,100,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 譯史安天合者，諂事鎮海，首引奧都剌合蠻撲買課稅，又增至二百二十萬兩。

translations.literal: The translator-clerk An Tianhe, who flattered Prince Zhenhai, first introduced Odu Laheman to monopolize tax purchase, raising it again to 2,200,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: The translator-clerk An Tianhe, who flattered Prince Zhenhai, introduced Odu Laheman to monopolize tax collection and raised the quota to 2,200,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 楚材極力辨諫，至聲色俱厲，言與涕俱。

translations.literal: Chucai argued and remonstrated with all his strength, until both voice and expression were severe, words mingled with tears.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai argued against it with all his strength until his voice shook and tears ran with his words.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「爾欲搏鬥耶？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Do you wish to wrestle?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Do you want to fight me?"

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「爾欲為百姓哭耶？

translations.literal: He also said, "Do you wish to weep for the common people?"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Do you want to weep for the people?"

sentences.zh: 姑令試行之。

translations.literal: For the moment let it be tried.
translations.idiomatic: Let it be tried for now.

sentences.zh: 」楚材力不能止，乃嘆息曰：「民之困窮，將自此始矣！」

translations.literal: Chucai could not stop it by force and sighed, "The people's hardship and poverty will begin from this!"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai could not stop it and sighed, "The people's suffering begins here!"

sentences.zh: 楚材嘗與諸王宴，醉臥車中，帝臨平野見之，直幸其營，登車，手撼之。

translations.literal: Chucai once feasted with the princes, drunk and sleeping in his carriage; the emperor came to the open plain, saw him, went straight to his camp, mounted the carriage, and shook him by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a feast with the princes Chucai drank until he fell asleep in his carriage. The emperor saw him on the plain, went straight to his camp, climbed into the carriage, and shook him awake.

sentences.zh: 楚材熟睡未醒，方怒其擾己，忽開目視，始知帝至，驚起謝，帝曰：「有酒獨醉，不與朕同樂耶？

translations.literal: Chucai was in deep sleep and had not awakened; he was just angry at being disturbed when he suddenly opened his eyes and saw—it was only then he knew the emperor had come. Startled, he rose to apologize. The emperor said, "You have wine and get drunk alone—will you not share the pleasure with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Still half asleep, Chucai was about to protest the disturbance when he opened his eyes and saw the emperor. He started up in alarm to apologize. The emperor said, "Drinking alone—will you not share the pleasure with me?"

sentences.zh: 」笑而去。

translations.literal: Laughing, he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Laughing, he left.

sentences.zh: 楚材不及冠帶，馳詣行宮，帝為置酒，極歡而罷。

translations.literal: Chucai, without time to don cap and belt, galloped to the traveling palace; the emperor set out wine for him, and they enjoyed themselves to the full before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai rode to the traveling palace without even fixing his cap and belt. The emperor set out wine, and they drank together in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 楚材當國日久，得祿分其親族，未嘗私以官。

translations.literal: Chucai had directed the state for a long time; he divided his salary among his kin and never privately gave them office.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai had governed for many years. He shared his salary with his kin but never gave them office through private favor.

sentences.zh: 行省劉敏從容言之，楚材曰：「睦親之義，但當資以金帛。

translations.literal: The regional secretary Liu Min spoke of this at ease; Chucai said, "In the principle of cherishing kin, one should only supply them with gold and silk."
translations.idiomatic: The regional secretary Liu Min mentioned this casually. Chucai said, "Kin should be supported with gold and silk alone."

sentences.zh: 若使從政而違法，吾不能徇私恩也。」

translations.literal: If they enter government and violate the law, I cannot show partiality for private affection."
translations.idiomatic: If they enter government and break the law, I cannot favor them out of private affection."

sentences.zh: 歲辛丑二月三日，帝疾篤，醫言脈已絕。

translations.literal: In the year xinchou, on the third day of the second month, the emperor's illness was grave; the physicians said his pulse had ceased.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the second month of the xinchou year the emperor fell gravely ill. The physicians said his pulse had stopped.

sentences.zh: 皇后不知所為，召楚材問之，對曰：「今任使非人，賣官鬻獄，囚系非辜者多。

translations.literal: The empress did not know what to do and summoned Chucai to ask; he replied, "Now appointments are of unworthy men, offices are sold and prisons traded, and many innocents are imprisoned."
translations.idiomatic: The empress did not know what to do and summoned Chucai. He said, "Unworthy men hold office, offices and judgments are sold, and many innocents languish in prison."

sentences.zh: 古人一言而善，熒惑退舍，請赦天下囚徒。

translations.literal: In antiquity one good word made the Fire Star withdraw—I beg that all prisoners under heaven be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity one good deed made Mars withdraw from its course. I beg a general pardon for all prisoners.

sentences.zh: 」後即欲行之，楚材曰：「非君命不可。

translations.literal: The empress then wished to carry it out immediately; Chucai said, "Without the ruler's command it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: The empress wished to act at once. Chucai said, "It cannot be done without the emperor's command."

sentences.zh: 」俄頃，帝少蘇，因入奏，請肆赦，帝已不能言，首肯之。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor revived slightly; Chucai therefore entered to memorialize and request a general pardon. The emperor could no longer speak but nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor revived slightly. Chucai entered and asked for a general pardon. The emperor could not speak but nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 是夜，醫者候脈復生，適宣讀赦書時也，翌日而瘳。

translations.literal: That night the physicians attending the pulse found it live again—just as the amnesty edict was being proclaimed—and the next day he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: That night the physicians found his pulse return—just as the amnesty was proclaimed—and the next day he recovered.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月四日，帝將出獵，楚材以太乙數推之，亟言其不可，左右皆曰：「不騎射，無以為樂。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the eleventh month of winter the emperor was about to go hunting; Chucai calculated by the Taiyi numbers and urgently said it could not be done. Those at his side all said, "Without riding and shooting there is no pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the eleventh month the emperor prepared to hunt. Chucai calculated by the Taiyi method and urgently warned against it. His attendants said, "Without riding and shooting, what pleasure is there?"

sentences.zh: 」獵五日，帝崩於行在所。

translations.literal: After five days of hunting the emperor died at the traveling residence.
translations.idiomatic: After five days of hunting the emperor died at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 皇后乃馬真氏稱制，崇信姦回，庶政多紊。

translations.literal: The empress, Töregene, assumed regency; she honored and trusted wicked men, and miscellaneous administration was much disordered.
translations.idiomatic: The empress Töregene assumed regency. She favored wicked men, and government fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 奧魯剌合蠻以貨得政柄，廷中悉畏附之。

translations.literal: Odu Laheman obtained political power through wealth; everyone at court feared and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Odu Laheman bought political power with wealth, and the whole court feared and followed him.

sentences.zh: 楚材面折廷爭，言人所難言，人皆危之。

translations.literal: Chucai confronted them directly in court debate, speaking what others found hard to speak; everyone feared for him.
translations.idiomatic: Chucai confronted them openly in court and spoke what others dared not say. Everyone feared for his safety.

sentences.zh: 癸卯五月，熒惑犯房，楚材奏曰：「當有驚擾，然訖無事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the year guimao Mars invaded the Room mansion; Chucai memorialized, "There will be alarm and disturbance, yet in the end nothing will happen."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the guimao year Mars invaded the Room mansion. Chucai said, "There will be alarm, but in the end no harm."

sentences.zh: 」居無何，朝廷用兵，事起倉卒，後遂令授甲選腹心，至欲西遷以避之。

translations.literal: Before long the court took up arms; the affair arose in haste, and later they ordered armor issued and trusted men selected, even wishing to move the capital west to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court mobilized for war in sudden haste. The regency ordered armor issued and trusted men chosen, and even considered moving the capital west to escape trouble.

sentences.zh: 楚材進曰：「朝廷天下根本，根本一搖，天下將亂。

translations.literal: Chucai advanced and said, "The court is the root of all under heaven; if the root is shaken, the realm will fall into chaos."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "The court is the root of the realm. Shake the root and the realm falls into chaos."

sentences.zh: 臣觀天道，必無患也。

translations.literal: I observe Heaven's Way—there will surely be no calamity."
translations.idiomatic: I read Heaven's signs. There will be no real calamity."

sentences.zh: 」後數日乃定。

translations.literal: Several days later matters settled.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the crisis passed.

sentences.zh: 後以御寶空紙付奧都剌合蠻，使自書填行之。

translations.literal: Later blank paper bearing the imperial seal was given to Odu Laheman, allowing him to write and fill it in himself for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Later the regency gave Odu Laheman blank sheets bearing the imperial seal so he could write edicts and execute them himself.

sentences.zh: 楚材曰：「天下者先帝之天下。

translations.literal: Chucai said, "All under heaven is the late emperor's realm."
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "The realm belongs to the late emperor."

sentences.zh: 朝廷自有憲章，今欲紊之，臣不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: The court has its own statutes and regulations; now you wish to disorder them—I dare not obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: The court has its own laws. To throw them into disorder now—I dare not obey."

sentences.zh: 」事遂止。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 又有旨：「凡奧都剌合蠻所建白，令史不為書者，斷其手。

translations.literal: There was also an order: "For all proposals made by Odu Laheman, if a clerk does not write them down, his hand is to be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Another order declared that any clerk who refused to record Odu Laheman's proposals would have his hand cut off.

sentences.zh: 」楚材曰：「國之典故，先帝悉委老臣，令史何與焉？

translations.literal: Chucai said, "The state's precedents and regulations the late emperor wholly entrusted to this old minister—what have clerks to do with them?"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai said, "State precedent was wholly entrusted to me by the late emperor. What have clerks to do with it?"

sentences.zh: 事若合理，自當奉行，如不可行，死且不避，況截手乎！

translations.literal: If a matter is reasonable I will naturally follow it; if it cannot be carried out, I do not avoid even death—how much less cutting off hands!
translations.idiomatic: If a proposal is sound I will follow it. If it is not, I will not shrink from death—much less from losing a hand!

sentences.zh: 」後不悅。

translations.literal: The empress was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was displeased.

sentences.zh: 楚材辨論不已，因大聲曰：「老臣事太祖、太宗三十餘年，無負于國，皇后亦豈能無罪殺臣也！

translations.literal: Chucai argued without cease and therefore said loudly, "This old minister served Taizu and Taizong for more than thirty years without failing the state—even the empress cannot kill me without cause!"
translations.idiomatic: Chucai argued on without stopping and finally cried out, "I served Taizu and Taizong for more than thirty years without failing the state. Even the empress cannot kill me without cause!"

sentences.zh: 」後雖憾之，亦以先朝舊勳，深敬憚焉。

translations.literal: Though the empress resented him, because he was an old meritorious official of the former reign she deeply respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Though she resented him, she deeply respected and feared him as a veteran of the founding reigns.

sentences.zh: 甲辰夏五月，薨於位，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer in the year jiachen he died in office at the age of fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer in the jiachen year he died in office at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 皇后哀悼，賻贈甚厚。

translations.literal: The empress mourned him and bestowed very generous funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress mourned him and gave lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 後有譖楚材者，言其在相位日久，天下貢賦，半入其家。

translations.literal: Later someone slandered Chucai, saying that during his long tenure in office half the realm's tribute and taxes entered his household.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone slandered him, claiming that during his long tenure half the empire's revenue had gone into his household.

sentences.zh: 後命近臣麻里扎覆視之，唯琴阮十餘，及古今書畫、金石、遺文數千卷。

translations.literal: The empress ordered the close minister Maliqa to reinspect; there were only a dozen or so qins and ruan, together with several thousand scrolls of ancient and modern calligraphy and painting, bronze and stone inscriptions, and surviving texts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress ordered the intimate Maliqa to reinspect his estate. He found only a dozen musical instruments and several thousand scrolls of books, paintings, and rubbings.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，贈經國議制寅亮佐運功臣、太師、上柱國，追封廣寧王，諡文正。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Deliberated on State Policy, Brought Brightness, and Assisted the Dynasty; Grand Preceptor; Upper Pillar of the State; was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangning; posthumous name Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously honored as grand preceptor and upper pillar of the state, enfeoffed as Prince of Guangning, and given the posthumous name Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 子鉉、鑄。

translations.literal: His sons were Xian and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xian and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 鑄字成仲，幼聰敏，善屬文，尤工騎射。

translations.literal: Zhu, style name Chengzhong, was clever as a child, skilled at composition, and especially adept at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, style Chengzhong, was clever as a boy, wrote well, and was especially skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 楚材薨，嗣領中書省事，時年二十三。

translations.literal: When Chucai died, Zhu succeeded to direct the affairs of the Secretariat at the age of twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: When Chucai died, Zhu succeeded him as head of the secretariat at the age of twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 鑄上言宜疏禁網，遂採歷代德政合於時宜者八十一章以進。

translations.literal: Zhu memorialized that the penal code should be relaxed and thereupon collected eighty-one items of virtuous governance from successive ages suited to the present time and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu memorialized that the penal code should be relaxed and presented eighty-one examples of humane governance from past dynasties suited to the present age.

sentences.zh: 戊午，憲宗徵蜀，詔鑄領侍衛驍果以從，屢出奇計，攻下城邑，賜以尚方金鎖甲及內厩驄馬。

translations.literal: In the year wuwu Emperor Xianzong campaigned against Shu; Zhu was ordered to lead the palace guard swift troops in attendance; he repeatedly devised unusual stratagems and captured walled cities; he was bestowed with imperial gold-linked armor and a piebald horse from the inner stables.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year Emperor Xianzong campaigned against Shu. Zhu led the palace guard in the field, devised repeated stratagems, and captured cities. He was rewarded with imperial gold-linked armor and a piebald horse from the royal stables.

sentences.zh: 乙未，憲宗崩，阿里不哥叛，鑄棄妻子，挺身自朔方來歸，世祖嘉其忠，即日召見，賞賜優厚。

translations.literal: In the year yiwei Emperor Xianzong died and Ariq Böke rebelled; Zhu abandoned wife and children and came alone from the northern frontier to submit; Shizu praised his loyalty, summoned him that same day, and rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year Emperor Xianzong died and Ariq Böke rebelled. Zhu abandoned his family and came alone from the north to submit. Kublai praised his loyalty, received him that same day, and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，拜中書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was appointed Left Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he was appointed left director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，詔將兵備禦北邊，後徵兵扈從，敗阿里不哥於上都之北。

translations.literal: That winter he was ordered to command troops to guard the northern frontier; later he was summoned with the army in attendance and defeated Ariq Böke north of Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was ordered to guard the northern frontier. Later he joined the imperial campaign and defeated Ariq Böke north of Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 奏定法令三十七章，吏民便之。

translations.literal: He memorialized and fixed thirty-seven articles of law; officials and people found them convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted thirty-seven legal articles that officials and commoners found convenient.

sentences.zh: 二年，行省山東。

translations.literal: In the second year he served as regional commissioner in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he served as regional commissioner in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 未幾徵還。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 初，清廟雅樂，止有登歌，詔鑄制宮懸八佾之舞。

translations.literal: Initially the refined music of the Pure Temple had only ascending song; Zhu was ordered to compose the palace orchestra music and the eight-rows dance.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court ritual music had only ascending hymns. Zhu was ordered to compose full orchestral music and the eight-rows dance.

sentences.zh: 四年春三月，樂舞成，表上之，仍請賜名《大成》，制曰「可」。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring in the fourth year the music and dance were completed; he memorialized and presented them, also requesting the title "Great Completion"; the edict said "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year the music and dance were finished. He presented them and asked that they be named Great Completion. The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 六月，改榮祿大夫、平章政事。
