translations.literal: In the sixth month he was changed to Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and Co-Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was made grand master for glorious blessing and co-director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年，復拜光祿大夫、中書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was again appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Left Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was again appointed grand master of splendid happiness and left director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷平章軍國重事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Co-Director of Important Military and Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made co-director of important military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔監修國史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to supervise compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to supervise compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有大事，必諮訪焉。

translations.literal: When the court had great affairs, it always consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: On every major matter the court consulted him.

sentences.zh: 十九年，復拜中書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was again appointed Left Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was again appointed left director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十年冬十月，坐不納職印、妄奏東平人聚謀為逆、間諜幕僚、及黨罪囚阿里沙，遂罷免，仍沒其家貲之半，徙居山後。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the twentieth year, on charges of not accepting the seal of office, falsely memorializing that people of Dongping had gathered to plot rebellion, spying through staff, and shielding the criminal prisoner Ali Sha, he was dismissed, half his household property was confiscated, and he was moved to live behind the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twentieth year he was dismissed for refusing his seal of office, falsely reporting a Dongping conspiracy, employing spies among his staff, and shielding the prisoner Ali Sha. Half his property was confiscated and he was exiled north of the Yan range.

sentences.zh: 二十二年卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died at the age of sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 子十一人：希徵，希勃，希亮，希寬，希素，希固，希周，希光，希逸淮東宣慰使，餘失其名。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons: Xizheng, Xibo, Xiliang, Xikuan, Xisu, Xigu, Xizhou, Xiguang, and Xiyi, Huaidong pacification commissioner—the rest have lost their names.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons: Xizheng, Xibo, Xiliang, Xikuan, Xisu, Xigu, Xizhou, Xiguang, and Xiyi, who became Huaidong pacification commissioner; the names of the rest are lost.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，贈推忠保德宣力佐治功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、懿寧王，諡文忠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously granted Meritorious Minister Who Promoted Loyalty, Preserved Virtue, and Assisted Governance; Grand Preceptor; Grand Guardian with equal ceremony to the Three Excellencies; Upper Pillar of the State; Prince of Yining; posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun he was posthumously honored as grand preceptor and prince of Yining with the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: ○粘合重山子南合

translations.literal: Nianhe Chongshan; appended: his son Nanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhe Chongshan; appended biography of his son Nanhe.

sentences.zh: 粘合重山，金源貴族也。

translations.literal: Nianhe Chongshan was a noble of the Jin source region.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhe Chongshan was a noble of the Jin frontier.

sentences.zh: 國初為質子，知金將亡，遂委質焉。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was a hostage; knowing that Jin would perish, he thereupon pledged himself to the new dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding years he was a hostage at the Mongol court. Seeing that Jin would fall, he pledged himself to the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜畜馬四百匹，使為宿衛官必阇赤。

translations.literal: Taizu bestowed four hundred horses for raising and appointed him a night-guard officer, beköchi.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu gave him four hundred horses and made him a night-guard officer, a beköchi.

sentences.zh: 從平諸國有功。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the various states and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the conquest of the various states.

sentences.zh: 圍涼州，執大旗指麾六軍，手中流矢，不動。

translations.literal: Besieging Liangzhou, he held the great banner and directed the six armies; an arrow struck his hand, yet he did not move.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Liangzhou he held the great banner and directed the armies. An arrow struck his hand, yet he did not stir.

sentences.zh: 已而為侍從官，數得侍宴內廷。

translations.literal: Before long he became an attendant officer and often attended banquets in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He later became an attendant and often joined banquets in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 因諫曰：「臣聞天子以天下為憂，憂之未有不治，忘憂未有能治者也。

translations.literal: He therefore remonstrated, saying, "I have heard that the Son of Heaven takes all under heaven as his worry—where there is worry there has never failed to be good order; where worry is forgotten there has never been able to be governance."
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated, "I have heard that a ruler who worries for the realm governs well, and one who forgets that worry cannot govern at all."

sentences.zh: 置酒為樂，此忘憂之術也。

translations.literal: Setting out wine for pleasure—this is the method of forgetting worry."
translations.idiomatic: Feasting for pleasure is a way to forget that worry."

sentences.zh: 」帝深嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply approved and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 立中書省，以重山有積勳，授左丞相。

translations.literal: When the Secretariat was established, because Chongshan had accumulated merit he was appointed Left Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the secretariat was established, Chongshan was appointed left director for his accumulated merit.

sentences.zh: 時耶律楚材為右丞相，凡建官立法，任賢使能，與夫分郡邑，定課賦，通漕運，足國用，多出楚材，而重山佐成之。

translations.literal: At the time Yelü Chucai was Right Director; establishing offices and making laws, appointing the worthy and employing the capable, as well as dividing commanderies and districts, fixing taxes and levies, opening grain transport by water, and filling state needs—all mostly came from Chucai, while Chongshan assisted in completing them.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Chucai was right director at the time. Most of the work of establishing offices, appointing talent, dividing commanderies, fixing taxes, opening transport, and filling the treasury came from Chucai, with Chongshan assisting.

sentences.zh: 太宗七年，從伐宋，詔軍前行中書省事，許以便宜。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taizong he followed the campaign against Song; he was ordered to direct Secretariat affairs before the army and was permitted discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's seventh year he joined the campaign against Song and was ordered to handle secretariat affairs with the army, with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 師入宋境，江淮州邑望風款附，重山降其民三十餘萬，取定城、天長二邑，不誅一人。

translations.literal: When the army entered Song territory, prefectures and districts along the Yangzi and Huai submitted at the first wind; Chongshan received the submission of more than three hundred thousand people, took the two districts Dingcheng and Tianchang, and executed not a single person.
translations.idiomatic: As the army entered Song territory, Yangzi and Huai prefectures submitted at once. Chongshan received the surrender of more than three hundred thousand people, took Dingcheng and Tianchang, and killed no one.

sentences.zh: 復入中書視事，賜中厩馬十匹、貫珠袍一。

translations.literal: He returned to the Secretariat to handle affairs and was bestowed ten horses from the central stables and one pearl-strung robe.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the secretariat and was rewarded with ten horses from the central stables and a pearl-strung robe.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉，封魏國公，諡忠武。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, posthumous name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made grand commandant, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, with the posthumous name Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: ○楊惟中

translations.literal: Yang Weizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhong.

sentences.zh: 楊惟中，字彥誠，弘州人。

translations.literal: Yang Weizhong, style name Yancheng, was a man of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhong, style Yancheng, was from Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 金末，以孤童子事太宗，知讀書，有膽略，太宗器之。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin, as a lone youth he served Taizong; he knew how to read and had courage and resourcefulness; Taizong valued him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jin he entered Taizong's service as a fatherless boy. He could read, showed courage and resource, and Taizong valued him.

sentences.zh: 年二十，奉命使西域三十餘國，宣暢國威，敷布政條，俾皆籍戶口屬吏，乃歸，帝於是有大用意。

translations.literal: At twenty he was ordered as envoy to more than thirty states of the Western Regions, proclaiming national might and spreading administrative regulations, causing all to register households and submit to officials; when he returned the emperor thereafter had great designs.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was sent as envoy to more than thirty Western Regions states to proclaim Mongol power, impose regulations, and register populations. When he returned the emperor formed great plans for the west.

sentences.zh: 皇子闊出伐宋，命惟中於軍前行中書省事。

translations.literal: When Prince Kökechu campaigned against Song, Weizhong was ordered to handle Secretariat affairs before the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kökechu campaigned against Song, Weizhong was ordered to handle secretariat affairs with the army.

sentences.zh: 克宋棗陽、光化等軍，光、隨、郢、復等州，及襄陽、德安府，凡得名士數十人，收伊、洛諸書送燕都，立宋大儒周惇頤祠，建太極書院，延儒士趙復、王粹等講授其間，遂通聖賢學，慨然欲以道濟天下。

translations.literal: He captured the Song armies of Zaoyang, Guanghua, and others, the prefectures Guang, Sui, Ying, Fu, and others, and the prefectures Xiangyang and De'an; in all he obtained several tens of eminent scholars, collected the books of the Yi and Luo regions and sent them to Yan capital, established a shrine to the great Song Confucian Zhou Dunyi, built the Taiji Academy, and invited Confucian scholars Zhao Fu, Wang Cui, and others to lecture there; he thereby penetrated the learning of the sages and worthies and sighed that he wished to save the world through the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Zaoyang, Guanghua, and other Song garrisons, together with Guang, Sui, Ying, Fu, Xiangyang, and De'an. He gathered several dozen eminent scholars, sent books from the Yi and Luo regions to Yan, built a shrine to Zhou Dunyi, founded the Taiji Academy, and invited Zhao Fu, Wang Cui, and other scholars to lecture there. He thus revived classical learning and hoped to save the world through the Way.

sentences.zh: 拜中書令，太宗崩，太后稱制，惟中以一相負任天下。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat; when Taizong died and the empress dowager assumed regency, Weizhong bore the weight of all under heaven as a single minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the secretariat. When Taizong died and the empress dowager assumed regency, Weizhong bore the weight of the realm alone as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 定宗即位，平陽道斷事官斜徹橫恣不法，詔惟中宣慰，惟中按誅之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dingzong ascended, the Pingyang Circuit judge Sheche was violent and lawless; Weizhong was ordered as pacification commissioner; he investigated and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dingzong ascended, the Pingyang judge Sheche ruled lawlessly. Weizhong was sent as pacification commissioner and had him executed after investigation.

sentences.zh: 金亡，其將武仙潰於鄧州，餘黨散入太原、真定間，據大明川，用金開興年號，眾至數万，剽掠數千里，詔會諸道兵討之，不克。

translations.literal: When Jin perished, its general Wu Xian was routed at Dengzhou; remnant bands scattered into the area between Taiyuan and Zhending, occupied Damingchuan, used Jin's Kaixing reign title, numbered tens of thousands, and plundered for several thousand li; an edict gathered troops from all circuits to attack them but they could not be overcome.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin fell, the general Wu Xian was routed at Dengzhou. Remnant bands scattered between Taiyuan and Zhending, held Damingchuan, used Jin's Kaixing reign title, and numbered tens of thousands, plundering for thousands of li. Troops from all circuits were summoned but could not defeat them.

sentences.zh: 惟中仗節開諭，降其渠帥，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Weizhong bore his staff and opened persuasion; the bandit chiefs submitted and the rest were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong went with imperial authority to persuade them. The chiefs submitted and the rest were pacified.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，世祖以太弟鎮金蓮川，得開府，專封拜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended, Shizu as imperial younger brother guarded Jinlianchuan, obtained an open office, and had exclusive authority to enfeoff and appoint.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong ascended, Kublai as imperial younger brother guarded Jinlianchuan with an open office and exclusive authority to appoint officials.

sentences.zh: 乃立河南道經略司於汴梁，奏惟中等為使，俾屯田唐、鄧、申、裕、嵩、汝、蔡、息、亳、潁諸州。

translations.literal: He thereupon established the Henan Circuit Pacification Commission at Bianliang, memorialized Weizhong and others as commissioners, and ordered them to open fields in the prefectures Tang, Deng, Shen, Yu, Song, Ru, Cai, Xi, Bo, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He established the Henan pacification commission at Bianliang and memorialized Weizhong as commissioner, ordering colonization in Tang, Deng, Shen, Yu, Song, Ru, Cai, Xi, Bo, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 初，滅金時，以監河橋萬戶劉福為河南道總管，福貪鄙殘酷，虐害遺民二十餘年。

translations.literal: Initially, when Jin was destroyed, Liu Fu, ten-thousand-household commander of Jianhe Bridge, was made Henan Circuit chief commander; Fu was greedy, base, and cruel, abusing the surviving people for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was destroyed, Liu Fu, commander of Jianhe Bridge, was made Henan chief commander. For more than twenty years he was greedy, cruel, and abusive toward the surviving population.

sentences.zh: 惟中至，召福聽約束，福稱疾不至，惟中設大梃於坐，復召之，使謂福曰：「汝不奉命，吾以軍法從事。

translations.literal: When Weizhong arrived he summoned Fu to hear his orders; Fu claimed illness and did not come; Weizhong set a great staff by his seat and summoned him again, sending word: "If you do not obey orders, I will deal with you by military law."
translations.idiomatic: When Weizhong arrived he summoned Fu to hear his orders. Fu claimed illness and stayed away. Weizhong placed a heavy staff by his seat and summoned him again, saying, "Disobey and I will deal with you by military law."

sentences.zh: 」福不得已，以數千人擁衛見惟中，惟中即握大梃擊僕之。

translations.literal: Fu had no choice; with several thousand men escorting him he came to see Weizhong; Weizhong immediately seized the great staff and struck down his servants.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had no choice but to come with several thousand guards. Weizhong seized the staff and beat down his attendants.

sentences.zh: 數日福死，河南大治。

translations.literal: Within several days Fu died and Henan was greatly governed.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Fu died, and Henan was well governed.

sentences.zh: 遷陝右四川宣撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi-right and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to pacification commissioner of Shaanxi-right and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍帥橫侈病民，郭千戶者尤甚，殺人之夫而奪其妻，惟中戮之以徇，關中肅然。

translations.literal: At the time army commanders were overbearing and extravagant, harming the people; a Commander Guo was especially so, killing a man's husband and seizing his wife; Weizhong executed him as a warning and Guanzhong became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Army commanders were oppressing the people. One Commander Guo was especially vicious, killing a husband and seizing his wife. Weizhong executed him as a warning, and Guanzhong became orderly.

sentences.zh: 語人曰：「吾非好殺，國家綱紀不立，致此輩賊害良民，無所控告，雖慾不去，可乎！

translations.literal: He told others, "I am not fond of killing; the state's discipline is not established, causing men like these to injure good people with none to appeal—though one wishes not to remove them, how can it be done!"
translations.idiomatic: He told others, "I do not love killing. When state discipline fails, such men prey on the innocent with no recourse. How can I leave them alone?"

sentences.zh: 」歲己未，世祖總統東師，奏惟中為江淮京湖南北路宣撫使，俾建行台，以先啟行，宣布恩信，蒙古、漢軍諸帥並聽節制。

translations.literal: In the year jiwei Shizu commanded the eastern army; he memorialized Weizhong as Pacification Commissioner of the Jianghuai, Jinghu, and Henan-north circuits, ordering him to establish a branch secretariat, go ahead to open the campaign, proclaim favor and trust, and all Mongol and Han army commanders were to obey his control.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year Kublai commanded the eastern army and memorialized Weizhong as pacification commissioner for the Jianghuai, Jinghu, and Henan-north circuits. He was to establish a branch secretariat, advance ahead to proclaim imperial favor, and all Mongol and Han commanders were placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 師還，卒於蔡州，年五十五。

translations.literal: When the army returned he died at Caizhou at the age of fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he died at Caizhou at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，追諡曰忠肅公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was posthumously given the title Duke Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he was posthumously titled Duke Zhongsu.
